item.title: Madbouly discusses AI investment with SandboxAQ chief Jack Hidary at WEF meeting
item.dc:creator: Daily News Egypt
item.description: Egyptian Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly met Jack Hidary, chief executive of SandboxAQ, on Tuesday to discuss investment and cooperation in artificial intelligence, on the sidelines of the World Economic Forum’s country strategy meeting on Egypt in the New Administrative Capital. Hidary is co-chair of the meeting. Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade Mohamed Farid Saleh […]
item.content:encoded:
Egyptian Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly met Jack Hidary, chief executive of SandboxAQ, on Tuesday to discuss investment and cooperation in artificial intelligence, on the sidelines of the World Economic Forum’s country strategy meeting on Egypt in the New Administrative Capital.

Hidary is co-chair of the meeting. Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade Mohamed Farid Saleh also attended.

Egypt’s AI strategy

Madbouly said AI was reshaping economies and societies, creating opportunities for entrepreneurship, productivity and growth, while raising challenges around governance, cybersecurity, data protection, digital infrastructure and labour markets.

He said Egypt had sought a national approach that balanced innovation with the responsible and safe use of the technology. He pointed to the first national AI strategy, launched in 2021, and the second edition covering 2025 to 2030, which he said goes beyond adopting AI applications to building a national industry able to develop the technology and make Egyptian companies more competitive.

The government is also working on a national AI governance framework for 2026, he said, and the National Council for Artificial Intelligence oversees the strategy’s implementation. Madbouly added that the state wanted to attract investment in large data centres.

SandboxAQ’s offer

Hidary said AI offered Egypt opportunities in trade, entrepreneurship, energy, scientific research and industry, and that SandboxAQ was ready to share its experience and models in these sectors. He cited Egypt’s digital infrastructure and skilled workforce, and said the company wanted to work with both the public and private sectors.

Farid said there were clear opportunities to work with SandboxAQ, to be developed with the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology and other bodies. Meetings would be arranged between company officials and their Egyptian counterparts during the team’s current visit, he said.

The two sides agreed to step up consultations on expanding the company’s presence in Egypt.

item.title: Misr Life Insurance to offer 15% stake on EGX in December
item.dc:creator: Daily News Egypt
item.description: Misr Life Insurance has announced its intention to proceed with an initial public offering (IPO) on the Egyptian Exchange (EGX), involving the sale of a 15% stake in the company, with subscription and trading expected to take place in December 2026. In a statement issued on Tuesday, the company said the offering would comprise 750 […]
item.content:encoded:
Misr Life Insurance has announced its intention to proceed with an initial public offering (IPO) on the Egyptian Exchange (EGX), involving the sale of a 15% stake in the company, with subscription and trading expected to take place in December 2026.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, the company said the offering would comprise 750 million existing ordinary shares, representing 15% of its issued share capital, held by Misr Insurance Holding Company, which is wholly owned by the Sovereign Fund of Egypt for Investment and Development.

The selling shareholder’s remaining stake will be subject to lock-up restrictions in accordance with applicable EGX listing rules and customary market practice.

The offering will comprise a private placement targeting qualified investors in Egypt and selected jurisdictions outside the United States, alongside a public offering open to investors in Egypt. Both tranches will be priced at the same per-share price, to be determined through a bookbuilding process.

The company is currently working to obtain the necessary approvals for the offering, including approval of the offering prospectus by the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA), registration of its shares with the authority and the relevant approvals from the EGX.

Subscription is expected to be completed and trading to commence in December 2026, subject to obtaining the necessary regulatory approvals and prevailing market conditions.

Misr Life Insurance has appointed EFG Hermes as the sole global coordinator and sole bookrunner for the offering.

White & Case has been appointed as the company’s international legal counsel, while Helmy, Hamza & Partners, a member of Baker McKenzie International, will serve as its Egyptian legal counsel.

Milbank and Zulficar & Partners Law Firm have been appointed as international and Egyptian legal counsel to EFG Hermes, respectively. Saleh, Barsoum & Abdel Aziz, a member firm of Grant Thornton International Ltd, serves as the company’s auditor.

Mostafa El-Kammash, Managing Director and CEO of Misr Life Insurance, said: “We are delighted to announce our intention to list Misr Life Insurance’s shares on the Egyptian Exchange, marking a milestone for a company that has protected Egyptian families and businesses for 126 years and representing the first major insurance company listing on the exchange.

“Misr Life Insurance is Egypt’s largest life insurer by assets, shareholders’ equity and profits. It has a nationwide multi-channel distribution platform, the largest investment portfolio in the sector, and a longstanding track record of profitable growth and consistent dividend distributions across economic cycles.”

The company added: “Life insurance penetration in Egypt remains extremely low. We have redesigned our products, distribution model and technology platform to capitalise on the structural growth opportunity offered by the market.

“We look forward to welcoming new shareholders alongside Misr Insurance Holding Company and its ultimate owner, the Sovereign Fund of Egypt, as Misr Life Insurance enters the next chapter of its journey as a publicly listed company.”

Government reviews valuation ahead of offering

On Monday, Hashem El-Sayed, Assistant to the Prime Minister and CEO of the State-Owned Enterprises Unit, held a meeting to review the methodology underpinning the fair value assessment of Misr Life Insurance’s shares.

The meeting formed part of efforts to complete the procedures preceding the offering and verify that the valuation principles and methodology comply with the standards issued by the FRA.

El-Sayed said the review aimed to assess the soundness of the valuation methodology and the financial and economic assumptions used, as well as the study’s compliance with the Egyptian Financial Valuation Standards issued by the authority.

It also seeks to ensure that the findings reflect the nature of the company’s business, its financial and operational position, and its performance indicators.

He noted that Misr Life Insurance is one of the leading companies in Egypt’s insurance market, with a broad customer base and a diversified portfolio of insurance products.

This underscores the importance of preparing a valuation study based on professional and objective principles that accurately reflects the company’s fair economic value and supports decision-making related to the offering, he added.

El-Sayed stressed that completing the procedures for offering a stake in the company forms part of the government’s efforts to accelerate implementation of its IPO programme, strengthen private-sector participation in economic activity and improve the efficiency of state-owned asset management in line with established governance, transparency and professional standards.

He also said listing companies on the stock market supports the government’s objectives of increasing the EGX’s market capitalisation, broadening the ownership base and providing citizens and investors with diverse investment opportunities through stakes in companies with strong economic fundamentals and promising growth prospects.

El-Sayed clarified that listing companies on the EGX does not necessarily entail their sale or the state’s divestment from them. Rather, it represents one of the tools for regulating the state’s role in economic activity, in line with the 2026-2030 State Ownership Policy Document.

This approach forms part of a broader vision aimed at identifying the sectors and activities in which state ownership should be concentrated, while creating greater scope for private-sector participation, broadening the ownership base and enabling Egyptian investors, including individuals, to participate in promising investment opportunities.

These efforts are intended to deepen the capital market and maximise the returns generated from state-owned assets.

item.title: SCZONE courts China’s Changsha zone for investment in batteries, desalination and EVs
item.dc:creator: Daily News Egypt
item.description: Mostafa Sheikhoun, chairperson of the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE), received a delegation from China’s Changsha Economic and Technological Development Zone (CETDZ) to discuss joint investment and the localisation of advanced industries. The delegation was led by Lai Kunming, deputy director of the CETDZ administrative committee. Ahmed Gamal, SCZONE vice chairperson for the southern sector, […]
item.content:encoded:
Mostafa Sheikhoun, chairperson of the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE), received a delegation from China’s Changsha Economic and Technological Development Zone (CETDZ) to discuss joint investment and the localisation of advanced industries.

The delegation was led by Lai Kunming, deputy director of the CETDZ administrative committee. Ahmed Gamal, SCZONE vice chairperson for the southern sector, also attended.

Sheikhoun presented the zone’s four industrial areas and six ports on the Red Sea and Mediterranean, and pointed to Egypt’s free trade agreements with more than 100 countries, which he said give access to 4 billion consumers. He also cited tax and customs exemptions, energy supply, trained labour and a digital one-stop shop.

He said SCZONE’s strategy focused on localising components for seawater desalination plants, solar energy storage batteries, wind turbines, cars and electric vehicles, alongside logistics, port development and infrastructure projects.

Sheikhoun said cooperation with Chinese businesses had been successful and called for it to be deepened so that companies could use the zone as a global export platform to overcome geopolitical challenges and supply chain disruption.

Lai said he had been impressed by the zone’s infrastructure and investment facilities. He said CETDZ would encourage major companies and industrial and logistics firms in Changsha to explore opportunities in SCZONE and to take part in projects in future industries and the green economy.

item.title: Egypt seeks to attract Singaporean industrial investments in smart manufacturing
item.dc:creator: Daily News Egypt
item.description: Egypt is seeking to attract new Singaporean industrial investments, particularly in smart manufacturing and technology-based industries, as part of efforts to deepen bilateral economic cooperation, promote technology transfer and expand the country’s industrial base. Minister of Industry Khaled Hashem met with Singaporean Ambassador to Egypt Dominic Goh to discuss ways to attract Singaporean industrial investments […]
item.content:encoded:
Egypt is seeking to attract new Singaporean industrial investments, particularly in smart manufacturing and technology-based industries, as part of efforts to deepen bilateral economic cooperation, promote technology transfer and expand the country’s industrial base.

Minister of Industry Khaled Hashem met with Singaporean Ambassador to Egypt Dominic Goh to discuss ways to attract Singaporean industrial investments to the Egyptian market in the coming period.

The meeting was attended by Ahmed Maghawry, Assistant Minister of Industry for International Cooperation, and Basel Arafat, Assistant Minister of Industry.

Hashem highlighted the longstanding relations between Egypt and Singapore, stressing the ministry’s interest in benefiting from Singapore’s advanced experience in smart manufacturing and technology-based industries and transferring these technologies to the Egyptian market.

He noted that Egypt is keen to expand cooperation with Singapore in industrial sectors that can facilitate technology transfer, enhance manufacturing capabilities and strengthen the competitiveness of local industries.

For his part, Goh reaffirmed Singapore’s commitment to strengthening cooperation with Egypt across various fields.

He revealed that four Singaporean companies are currently operating in Egypt in the agricultural and food industries, fertilisers and shipping services. These companies use Egypt as a manufacturing and export hub to serve various international markets.

The ambassador also invited Hashem to visit Singapore and meet with Singaporean companies to encourage them to explore new investment opportunities and inject further investments into the Egyptian market.

item.title: FRA showcases Egypt’s non-banking finance experience to Sudanese delegation
item.dc:creator: Daily News Egypt
item.description: The Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) received a delegation from Sudan comprising officials from the Ministry of Finance, the Taxation Chamber and the Central Bank of Sudan to familiarise them with Egypt’s experience in regulating non-banking financial activities serving micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). The delegation was received by Rehab Taha, FRA Assistant Chairperson, who […]
item.content:encoded:
The Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) received a delegation from Sudan comprising officials from the Ministry of Finance, the Taxation Chamber and the Central Bank of Sudan to familiarise them with Egypt’s experience in regulating non-banking financial activities serving micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs).

The delegation was received by Rehab Taha, FRA Assistant Chairperson, who reaffirmed the Authority’s commitment to strengthening cooperation and exchanging expertise with counterpart institutions in Arab and African countries. She highlighted Egypt’s experience in developing regulatory and supervisory frameworks that support enterprise growth and expand access to financing.

The visit included a specialised training programme covering the FRA’s mandate and its role in supervising MSME financing activities, the regulatory developments the sector has undergone in recent years, and the supervisory and oversight tools applied to entities operating in the field.

The programme also introduced the Sudanese officials to the rules governing enterprise classification, licensing requirements, and the regulations and standards for conducting MSME financing activities, as well as mechanisms for customer protection.

FRA officials outlined the regulatory framework governing civil associations and institutions operating in the financing sector, including their classifications and licensing requirements. They also presented key market indicators highlighting the sector’s growing importance to the national economy and its capacity to support the expansion of small and medium-sized enterprises in governorates beyond major urban centres, while meeting the financing needs of millions of beneficiaries.

The sessions were delivered by Hossam Beshir, Supervisor of the Central Department for MSME Financing; Amal Salah, Deputy Head of the Central Department; and Ahmed Abdelaty, Executive Director of the Microfinance Activity Supervision Unit. They explained the sector’s regulatory and supervisory framework and responded to questions from members of the Sudanese delegation.

The visit forms part of ongoing cooperation between the FRA and its counterpart institutions and authorities in Arab countries, aimed at exchanging regulatory and supervisory expertise and jointly advancing non-banking financial activities, particularly MSME financing, to strengthen their contribution to sustainable development.

item.title: Essmat discusses bringing offshore wind to Egypt with CIP on sidelines of WEF meeting
item.dc:creator: Daily News Egypt
item.description: Egypt’s Minister of Electricity and Renewable Energy Mahmoud Essmat met Robert Helms, a partner and board member at CIP, to discuss new investment and introducing offshore wind technology to Egypt, on the sidelines of the World Economic Forum’s strategic meeting on Egypt. The meeting, opened on Tuesday by President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi, was attended by […]
item.content:encoded:
Egypt’s Minister of Electricity and Renewable Energy Mahmoud Essmat met Robert Helms, a partner and board member at CIP, to discuss new investment and introducing offshore wind technology to Egypt, on the sidelines of the World Economic Forum’s strategic meeting on Egypt.

The meeting, opened on Tuesday by President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi, was attended by Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly, Central Bank of Egypt Governor Hassan Abdalla, ministers and Egyptian and foreign business leaders.

Helms is responsible for offshore wind development and investment for CIP’s growth markets fund, which targets renewable energy infrastructure in high-growth economies. Mona Rizk, head of the Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company, also attended the talks.

CIP’s portfolio

The two sides reviewed CIP’s work in offshore and onshore wind, solar power, energy storage, electricity transmission and distribution, and biofuels. According to the ministry, the group manages 15 investment funds financing 150,000 MW of renewable energy projects worldwide.

Egypt’s renewables plan

The meeting covered the electricity sector’s plan to add about 32,000 MW of solar and wind capacity by 2030, with a wider use of battery storage, as Egypt seeks to reduce its reliance on conventional fuels.

They also discussed upgrading the transmission network to absorb the growing volume of renewable power, including work with international consultancies to assess what the national grid needs to integrate it.

Essmat said Egypt was integrating smart grid technologies and exploring the latest energy storage solutions.

Regional interconnection

The minister pointed to Egypt’s existing electricity links with Jordan, Libya and Sudan and the planned interconnection with Saudi Arabia.

He said studies were being finalised for a link to Europe via Greece to export 3,000 MW of renewable power, and for another link with Italy, as part of efforts to position Egypt as an energy bridge between Africa and Europe.

item.title: Opella Egypt trains 190 pharmacy students in third year of UpGrads programme
item.dc:creator: Daily News Egypt
item.description: Opella Egypt has completed the 2026 edition of its UpGrads internship programme, training 190 pharmacy students from around 42 faculties of pharmacy across the country. The programme, now in its third year, has reached 420 pharmacy students and graduates since its launch. This year’s UpGrads 3.0 summer internship took in 120 undergraduates in earlier years […]
item.content:encoded:
Opella Egypt has completed the 2026 edition of its UpGrads internship programme, training 190 pharmacy students from around 42 faculties of pharmacy across the country.

The programme, now in its third year, has reached 420 pharmacy students and graduates since its launch.

This year’s UpGrads 3.0 summer internship took in 120 undergraduates in earlier years of study, who attended workshops, field activities and mentoring sessions on the consumer healthcare industry. A further 70 final-year students spent six weeks on practical assignments under the guidance of company staff.

Participants came from faculties in Cairo, Giza, the Delta, Upper Egypt, Alexandria and the Canal cities.

“The move from university to work is a big step. Students need the chance to test their knowledge, build confidence and discover where their skills can take them,” said Ahmed El Kamhawy, Opella Egypt’s country head.

The programme forms part of Opella’s global target of training 200,000 pharmacists by 2030.

item.title: Lulu Group opens new hypermarket in Obour City, plans further expansion in Egypt
item.dc:creator: Daily News Egypt
item.description: Lulu Group has expanded its retail presence in Egypt with the opening of a new hypermarket in Obour City, Cairo, as the group continues to strengthen its footprint in the Egyptian market and pursue further expansion. The hypermarket was inaugurated by Hossam El Garrahi, Deputy to the Minister of Supply and Internal Trade and Chairperson […]
item.content:encoded:
Lulu Group has expanded its retail presence in Egypt with the opening of a new hypermarket in Obour City, Cairo, as the group continues to strengthen its footprint in the Egyptian market and pursue further expansion.

The hypermarket was inaugurated by Hossam El Garrahi, Deputy to the Minister of Supply and Internal Trade and Chairperson of the Internal Trade Development Authority (ITDA), in the presence of Hamad Obaid Ibrahim Salem Al Zaabi, UAE Ambassador to Egypt, and Yusuffali M.A., Chairperson of Lulu Group.

Commenting on the opening, Yusuffali said the new hypermarket represents another step in the group’s expansion in Egypt, expressing his appreciation for the Egyptian government’s continued support.

He reaffirmed Lulu’s commitment to investing in the Egyptian market, offering customers quality products at competitive prices and creating additional employment opportunities. He added that several new projects were in the pipeline as the group seeks to expand its presence across the country.

Spanning approximately 106,000 square feet, the new hypermarket offers a wide range of products, including groceries, fresh fruits and vegetables, fresh food, bakery products, electronics, home appliances and fashion accessories.

The facility also features dedicated parking areas and self-checkout counters to enhance customer convenience and streamline the shopping experience.

The inauguration was also attended by Ashraf Ali M.A., Executive Director of Lulu Group; Mohamed Althaf, Group Director – Global Operations and Chief Sustainability Officer; Anand Ram, Chief Operating Officer of Lulu International Holdings; and Shabu Abdul Majeed, Director of Lulu Global Operations, alongside other officials and representatives.

item.title: Syngenta invests $1.5bn annually in R&D, identifies Egypt as key Middle East market
item.dc:creator: Daily News Egypt
item.description: Agri-tech leader Syngenta is positioning Egypt as a key market in its Middle East strategy, building on the role of its KAHA research hub in developing agricultural solutions tailored to local farming conditions, as the company expands its regional partnerships and strengthens its presence across the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries and the Levant. Ülkü […]
item.content:encoded:
Agri-tech leader Syngenta is positioning Egypt as a key market in its Middle East strategy, building on the role of its KAHA research hub in developing agricultural solutions tailored to local farming conditions, as the company expands its regional partnerships and strengthens its presence across the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries and the Levant.

Ülkü Schmithüsen, General Manager and Business Area Head for the Middle East at Syngenta, told Daily News Egypt that the company invests more than $1.5bn annually in research and development (R&D) worldwide, covering innovation in crop protection, seeds and agricultural technologies, as well as digital solutions designed to address farmers’ needs.

She described the Middle East as an important region for Syngenta, noting that the company operates in 15 countries, with Egypt representing one of its key markets. Its regional presence also extends across the Levant and GCC, both of which remain central to its expansion strategy.

Regarding financial performance, Schmithüsen said Syngenta’s crop protection business recorded sales of approximately $2bn across Asia, the Middle East and Africa in 2025. However, she noted that, as a privately held company, Syngenta does not publicly disclose its projected growth rates.

She stressed that partnerships are essential to strengthening the company’s capabilities and expanding the reach of its solutions, adding that no single company can address the challenges facing agriculture independently. Syngenta therefore regularly explores regional partnerships that can deliver tangible benefits to farmers.

Supply chains and manufacturing strategy

Asked whether Syngenta was considering relocating a larger share of its production operations or supply chains to regional markets to reduce dependence on imports, Schmithüsen said the company’s priority was to ensure reliable access to the products and solutions farmers need.

She added that Syngenta had developed a robust and diversified supply chain, allowing it to respond flexibly to customer requirements across global markets.

On the possibility of Egypt becoming a regional manufacturing and distribution hub for agricultural inputs serving Africa and the Middle East, she explained that producing active ingredients for crop protection products is a highly complex process requiring specialised expertise, advanced technologies and stringent quality controls.

For reasons of efficiency and safety, Syngenta centralises production at a limited number of facilities worldwide and exports its products to more than 90 countries, she said.

Research capabilities and agricultural land

Regarding the company’s ownership of agricultural land for research, development or commercial production, Schmithüsen said Syngenta did not own land in the Middle East.

She highlighted the role of the company’s KAHA research facility in Egypt, which provides local R&D capabilities and develops solutions tailored to the specific conditions and needs of Egyptian agriculture.

However, the executive did not disclose details of the group’s total global land holdings, the areas it owns or manages, or whether it was considering investments in experimental or commercial farms in the Middle East.

Syngenta’s regional strategy combines local research capabilities, partnerships with regional entities and a global production and distribution network, with Egypt playing an important role through both its market presence and research activities.

item.title: Al-Sisi: Egypt’s IMF programme nears completion as economy grows 5.1% in FY2025/26
item.dc:creator: Daily News Egypt
item.description: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi said on Tuesday that Egypt’s cooperation programme with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) was nearing completion, citing economic growth of 5.1% in the 2025/26 fiscal year, foreign reserves of $57.5bn in October and foreign direct investment (FDI) of approximately $18bn. Al-Sisi made the remarks during a high-level strategic dialogue at […]
item.content:encoded:
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi said on Tuesday that Egypt’s cooperation programme with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) was nearing completion, citing economic growth of 5.1% in the 2025/26 fiscal year, foreign reserves of $57.5bn in October and foreign direct investment (FDI) of approximately $18bn.

Al-Sisi made the remarks during a high-level strategic dialogue at an Egypt-focused meeting organised by the World Economic Forum (WEF) in Cairo on November 16–17, attended by representatives of around 80 major companies and multilateral financial institutions.

The president said Egypt had implemented economic reform programmes over the past 12 years in cooperation with international institutions, particularly the IMF, adding that the country had met programme targets despite what he described as the significant costs borne by Egyptians.

He said the next phase would focus on boosting economic productivity, expanding the private sector’s role and integrating the economy more deeply into regional and global value chains through a national transformation programme for 2027-2030, scheduled to be announced in December.

Al-Sisi said Egypt aimed to establish itself as an industrial, production and export hub by localising industries, transferring technology and increasing local content.

Egypt’s 2030 industrial strategy targets raising manufacturing’s contribution to gross domestic product (GDP) to 20%, with green industries accounting for 5%, he said.

Private-sector investment increased by 25.9% in the first quarter of the 2025/26 fiscal year, accounting for 66% of total investment, Al-Sisi said, citing ongoing efforts to implement the State Ownership Policy and expand the role of private companies in economic activity.

He said Egypt was offering incentives in priority sectors, including clean energy, automotive manufacturing and electric vehicles, pharmaceuticals, solar-panel production, and information and communications technology (ICT).

Al-Sisi also highlighted the government’s golden licence programme and said customs reforms had reduced average cargo clearance times to two days. The government is also developing a unified digital platform for businesses, he added.

Energy expansion and regional ambitions

On energy, Al-Sisi said Egypt’s electricity generation capacity had increased from around 28 gigawatts (GW) to approximately 64 GW, while the country was targeting a renewable energy share of 45% by 2028.

Egypt is also expanding electricity interconnections with neighbouring countries, as well as Greece, Italy and Cyprus, he said.

The president said Egypt sought to strengthen its position as a regional energy hub for the eastern Mediterranean and Africa, drawing on its gas and electricity networks, liquefied natural gas (LNG) facilities in Idku and Damietta, refineries and port infrastructure.

He said Egypt had fully settled its arrears to foreign oil and gas partners by June 30, 2026, and was working with Cyprus on plans to transport Cypriot gas to Egypt’s LNG facilities for re-export to European markets by 2028.

Al-Sisi said the adoption of a flexible exchange rate had helped ease foreign currency shortages and address difficulties previously faced by foreign investors in repatriating capital and profits.

Foreign investors could now transfer their profits abroad and obtain foreign currency through the banking system to finance imports, he added.

Infrastructure and Suez Canal recovery

On infrastructure, Al-Sisi said Egypt’s inhabited and developed land area had doubled from approximately 7% to 14%, while the number of new cities had increased from 22 to 61.

The country’s main road network now exceeds 30,000 kilometres, he said, adding that the state spends around EGP 1trn annually on infrastructure, including ports, airports, logistics centres and facilities for storing strategic commodities and fuel.

Al-Sisi said Egypt had lost approximately $20 billion in Suez Canal revenues over recent years because of regional crises, but noted that shipping traffic through the waterway was recovering.

He also said developments involving Iran and the Strait of Hormuz had influenced thinking about logistics hubs and international trade routes.

The president said recent crises had reinforced the Suez Canal’s importance to global trade, arguing that alternative transport routes could complement, but not replace, the waterway.

Around 12% of global trade passes through the Suez Canal, he said, adding that Egypt’s expanded ports and logistics corridors strengthened its position as a link between Asia, Europe and Africa.

Al-Sisi also highlighted opportunities for Egyptian and international companies to cooperate on infrastructure projects across Africa, citing Egyptian involvement in Tanzania’s Julius Nyerere hydropower project, the Jiji and Mulembwe hydropower projects in Burundi, and the Moheli port project in Comoros.

AI and digital infrastructure

On artificial intelligence (AI), Al-Sisi said Egypt had recently issued the second version of its national AI strategy and was expanding its digital infrastructure, data centres and cloud computing capabilities.

He said the country was seeking investment in data centres, cloud computing, the development of AI models and algorithms, research and development, and innovation centres.

Egypt now has 131 universities, Al-Sisi said, adding that efforts were focused on equipping graduates with the skills required in artificial intelligence, digital technologies and the evolving labour market.

During a discussion with international business leaders, Al-Sisi said investors could be confident in Egypt, citing what he described as political and economic stability, infrastructure development, and regulatory and tax reforms.

Participants raised questions about Egypt’s investment climate and opportunities in trade, manufacturing, renewable energy, artificial intelligence and digital infrastructure.
